_comment: Living taste profile for the wine-buying skill. Grows as verdicts get logged in cellar.jsonl. likes/dislikes are style-level signals; benchmarks are named reference bottles; notes is free-text. Edit by hand or let the buying/feedback skills append.
likes: STRUCTURE SHAPE: a rich, concentrated attack up front followed by a long tannic tail. Stated plainly as 'the ticket' (Fleur Cardinale 2020). Tannin as structure/grip is a positive — it is NOT what he means when he objects to bitterness.

Distinctive aromatics — especially floral perfume and novel blood-orange lift — are exciting positives, as is clean minerality. The palate still needs enough body and persistence to sustain the wine after the nose adapts.

Savory, structured Southern Rhône GSM / Châteauneuf-du-Pape reds — Mourvèdre-forward meatiness, stony power, garrigue. Confirmed sweet spot; excellent with red meat (steak). A broad, self-identified love of CdP/GSM.

Savory Left Bank Graves / Pessac-Leognan reds (Cab Sauv + Merlot on gravel): supple, silky, and with a 30-45 min decant a lovely floral perfume that carries into a cohesive palate. Integrated mineral bitterness is a PLUS here.
Plush, fruit-forward Right Bank Merlot (velvety black cherry/plum, cocoa, easy roundness) — tasty and crowd-friendly.
dislikes: UNINTEGRATED bitterness: a true-bitter 'bitter-almond' spike on the finish that sits disjointed over a lighter mid-palate/body (seen in Lalande-de-Pomerol; amplified by Cabernet Franc). NOTE: neither bitterness nor limestone is the problem on its own — a concentrated limestone St-Emilion (Fleur Cardinale 2020) and a big Mourvèdre-led CdP (Beaucastel 2023) both carried a bitter-almond finish happily. The problem is specifically a bitter/tannic finish the wine's body is too light to carry.
AROMATICS WITHOUT PALATE WEIGHT: perfume can impress at first, but once the nose adapts, a lighter body leaves too little on the tongue to sustain interest through the glass (Joanin Becot 2022).
benchmarks: Chateau de Rochemorin 2019 (Pessac-Leognan) = LOVE. Floral perfume + supple/silky texture + integrated mineral bitterness, cohesive. Reference for 'bitterness done right'. Decant 30-45 min to unlock the perfume.

Château de Beaucastel Châteauneuf-du-Pape 2023 (Southern Rhône, ~40% Mourvèdre) = LOVE. Mourvèdre-forward meatiness, killer with steak; the bitter-almond finish INTEGRATED after a ~30 min rest. Reference for savory Rhône GSM, and for patience unlocking a wine. Drunk out at a restaurant, not from the cellar.

Chateau Fleur Cardinale 2020 (St-Emilion Grand Cru Classe) = LIKE. Rich concentrated attack with a lengthy tannic tail — the structure shape he explicitly wants. Proves weighty limestone St-Emilion is fine; 14.5% abv, 90% new oak, dense.

Chateau Joanin Becot 2022 (Castillon Cotes de Bordeaux) = LIKE. Lovely perfume, a novel blood-orange note, and good minerality, but the body was a bit lacking; once the nose adapted, the palate did not sustain the second half of the second glass. Reference for aromatics outperforming body.

Chateau Garraud 2019 (Lalande-de-Pomerol) = LIKE (flawed). The cautionary version: tasty but the bitter-almond finish was jarring/disjointed against a lighter body. Reference for the finish that does NOT work.
notes: KEY TASTE AXIS: it is about BODY-TO-FINISH AND AROMATICS-TO-PALATE BALANCE, not about bitterness, tannin, limestone, or perfume as such. He likes a rich concentrated front end with a long tannic/mineral tail, and he values distinctive perfume and blood-orange lift when the palate has enough weight to remain compelling after the nose adapts. Five verdicts agree: the three wines with an assertive finish AND real concentration succeeded (Rochemorin, Beaucastel, Fleur Cardinale); Garraud's finish outweighed its lighter body, while Joanin Becot's beautiful perfume and minerality outperformed its lighter palate by the second glass. Buying implications: (1) Prioritize CONCENTRATION, mid-palate weight, and persistence — an under-powered wine is the failure mode whether the dominant attraction is its finish or its nose. (2) Do NOT avoid limestone Right Bank, Cabernet Franc, or tannic wines per se; earlier guidance to steer away from limestone was too broad and has been withdrawn. (3) GIVE IT TIME — a 30-45 min decant or rest unlocked two wines (Rochemorin's perfume from a tight start; Beaucastel's finish integrating), but air cannot manufacture missing body. (4) Confirmed sweet spots: savory Left Bank Graves/Pessac-Leognan, and savory Mourvèdre-forward Southern Rhône GSM/Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Verdicts so far: Rochemorin 2019 (love), Beaucastel CdP 2023 (love), Fleur Cardinale 2020 (like), Joanin Becot 2022 (like), Garraud 2019 (like-but-flawed).
